paper_cards.title: PhysLDM: Latent Diffusion for High-Fidelity Deformable Simulation
paper_cards.data: Objaverse-scale kinematic volumetric-mesh trajectories, with OOD evaluation on GSO and Toys4K.
paper_cards.method: A holistic spatiotemporal VAE compresses high-resolution volumetric trajectories, followed by latent diffusion for one-shot deformable dynamics prediction.
paper_cards.task: Predict long-horizon, high-resolution deformable-body trajectories and support differentiable inverse/design optimization.
paper_cards.novelty: Introduces a compact spatiotemporal latent-diffusion formulation for volumetric deformable simulation and shows diffusion avoids non-physical regression averages in chaotic regimes.
evidence: The paper reports about 2.48 mm reconstruction precision, up to 78x token compression, and zero-shot transfer to GSO and Toys4K.

claim_checks.claim: The paper reports about 2.48 mm reconstruction precision, up to 78x token compression, and zero-shot transfer to GSO and Toys4K.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Directly informs DeformableState, VolumetricMesh, MaterialDynamics, BoundaryCondition, and differentiable simulator interfaces.

paper_cards.title: WorldCast: Distributed Multiplayer World Models
paper_cards.data: Counter-Strike 2 multi-player trajectories with player positions, map geometry, controls, and synchronized views.
paper_cards.method: Each player runs a local video-generator/state-model client; clients exchange compact player and scene states projected into camera-aligned fields.
paper_cards.task: Generate independently controlled, mutually consistent multiplayer views in real time.
paper_cards.novelty: Replaces costly joint multi-view generation with distributed local world-model clients coordinated through compact shared state.
evidence: The paper reports over an order-of-magnitude gain in player rendering rate over joint generation and real-time scaling to four-player generation.

claim_checks.claim: The paper reports over an order-of-magnitude gain in player rendering rate over joint generation and real-time scaling to four-player generation.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Useful for SharedWorldState, PlayerState, CrossViewConsistency, ConcurrentAction, and distributed interactive-world runtime contracts.

paper_cards.title: Tetris3D: 3D Scene Generation With Objects That Fit Together
paper_cards.data: ComOb, a physics-simulation dataset of 1.2M scenes with per-object meshes and pairwise physical-relation annotations.
paper_cards.method: Generates each scene object conditioned on surrounding geometry and physical relations so shape and pose remain compatible at occluded interaction regions.
paper_cards.task: Reconstruct physically and geometrically coherent object-level 3D scenes from a single image.
paper_cards.novelty: Makes local inter-object fit an explicit generation condition rather than generating scene objects independently.
evidence: The authors report state-of-the-art generation quality and physical stability on synthetic and real-world scene evaluations.

claim_checks.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art generation quality and physical stability on synthetic and real-world scene evaluations.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct reference for ContactRelation, Support, FitConstraint, OccludedGeometry, PhysicalStability, and scene-assembly validators.

paper_cards.title: Never Look Back: Understanding Persistence in 3D Object Memory from Egocentric Videos
paper_cards.data: HD-EPIC, UCS-Bench, Ego4D, and 100 stitched multi-scene egocentric streams.
paper_cards.method: Ledger associates object observations into persistent 3D records, clusters resting locations, confirms moves with repeated evidence, and stores contextual descriptions.
paper_cards.task: Answer later spatial/object-state questions without replaying the original egocentric video.
paper_cards.novelty: Combines persistent 3D localization, object histories, and contextual descriptions while retaining untouched and out-of-view objects.
evidence: Ledger raises HD-EPIC accuracy from 29.7% to 42.6%, UCS-Bench from 33.8% to 38.5%, and reports 0.99 m median Ego4D localization error.

claim_checks.claim: Ledger raises HD-EPIC accuracy from 29.7% to 42.6%, UCS-Bench from 33.8% to 38.5%, and reports 0.99 m median Ego4D localization error.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Provides concrete PersistentObject, RestingLocation, MoveEvent, ContainerState, ObservationHistory, and retrieval fields.

paper_cards.title: DreamTrue: Action-Faithful Robot World Model with Counterfactual Post-Training
paper_cards.data: Multi-view AgiBot and cross-embodiment robot video plus a human-annotated interaction-defect reward dataset.
paper_cards.method: Image-space action trajectories and offline calibration improve action alignment; counterfactual actions broaden failures; an embodied video reward model guides RL post-training.
paper_cards.task: Predict physically plausible, action-faithful multi-view robot futures across embodiments.
paper_cards.novelty: Targets success bias in robot video data through counterfactual action post-training and explicit human-rated interaction defects.
evidence: The paper reports reducing human-assessed interaction defects from 48.12% to 6.25% and first place in the AgiBot World Challenge 2026 world-model track.

claim_checks.claim: The paper reports reducing human-assessed interaction defects from 48.12% to 6.25% and first place in the AgiBot World Challenge 2026 world-model track.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Strong reference for ActionTrajectory, Calibration, CounterfactualOutcome, InteractionDefect, and world-model reward interfaces.

paper_cards.title: PLaW-VLA: Predictive Latent World Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Policies
paper_cards.data: RoboTwin Hard Horizon III, LIBERO-Plus, and long-horizon manipulation trajectories.
paper_cards.method: A Mixture-of-Transformers predicts task-relevant future states in a pretrained latent space and conditions action generation via causal attention.
paper_cards.task: Use lightweight future prediction to improve long-horizon VLA control and distribution-shift generalization.
paper_cards.novelty: Models task-relevant predictive latents instead of reconstructing pixels, cutting world-model inference cost while preserving policy gains.
evidence: The paper reports +11.8 points over reactive policies on RoboTwin Hard Horizon III and about 1/19 the latency of generative WAM inference.

claim_checks.claim: The paper reports +11.8 points over reactive policies on RoboTwin Hard Horizon III and about 1/19 the latency of generative WAM inference.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Useful baseline for FutureLatent, TaskSemantics, CausalConditioning, Horizon, and long-horizon control evaluation.

paper_cards.title: UNITAS: A 3D-Native World Action Model for Embodied Manipulation
paper_cards.data: RoboTwin, LIBERO, real-world tasks, and mixed human-hand/robot interaction data.
paper_cards.method: Unifies visual observations, action flow, and scene flow in a metric 3D frame using point trajectories, scene displacements, and world-aligned embeddings.
paper_cards.task: Jointly generate executable actions and action-conditioned 3D scene evolution across hands and robot embodiments.
paper_cards.novelty: Moves WAM representation from view-dependent pixels to a shared metric 3D motion interface.
evidence: The paper reports up to 49% lower scene-displacement error than PointWorld, 99.8% LIBERO success, and 85% average real-world success.

claim_checks.claim: The paper reports up to 49% lower scene-displacement error than PointWorld, 99.8% LIBERO success, and 85% average real-world success.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct reference for MetricFrame, ActionFlow, SceneFlow, PointTrajectory, PhysicalTime, and cross-embodiment action schemas.

paper_cards.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
paper_cards.data: Large-scale real robot data spanning 12 embodiments, with released checkpoints and robot-deployment code.
paper_cards.method: An 8B-parameter JEPA predictor learns latent rollouts; second-order compute scaling laws link imagination error to downstream planning performance.
paper_cards.task: Predict latent robot futures and plan zero-shot toward goal images on real hardware.
paper_cards.novelty: Establishes empirical scaling laws for multi-embodiment latent robot world models and validates imagination error as a real-robot proxy.
evidence: The paper reports predictable power-law improvement with compute and zero-shot real-hardware planning; checkpoints and deployment code are released.

claim_checks.claim: The paper reports predictable power-law improvement with compute and zero-shot real-hardware planning; checkpoints and deployment code are released.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Useful for LatentRollout, ImaginationError, ComputeBudget, Embodiment, GoalImage, and scaling-law evaluation.

paper_cards.title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models
paper_cards.data: Robot and egocentric video, RoboCasa GR-1, LIBERO-Long, RoboTwin 2.0, DOMINO, Unitree G1, and YAM deployments.
paper_cards.method: Causal autoregressive pretraining is preserved during WAM adaptation, with streaming encoding, asynchronous execution, and hardware-specific acceleration.
paper_cards.task: Use long visual histories for responsive, dynamic, long-horizon manipulation.
paper_cards.novelty: Shows long context benefits depend on autoregressive video foundations and packages that history into a real-time WAM system.
evidence: The paper reports GR-1 success rising from 63.3% to 78.7% with 19.2 s context and 95% success on dynamic cup stacking.

claim_checks.claim: The paper reports GR-1 success rising from 63.3% to 78.7% with 19.2 s context and 95% success on dynamic cup stacking.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct baseline for ObservationHistory, ProgressState, StreamingEncoder, AsyncExecution, ContextLength, and latency-aware control.

paper_cards.title: DepthWorld: 3D World Model for Robot Manipulation
paper_cards.data: DROID-3D, a calibrated derivative of DROID with dense metric depth and recalibrated multi-view extrinsics.
paper_cards.method: Joint factor-graph calibration pools episodes from each robot, then a tiled Stable Video Diffusion model predicts multi-view RGB and metric depth.
paper_cards.task: Generate geometrically consistent action-conditioned robot futures for planning and evaluation.
paper_cards.novelty: Adds large-scale metric 3D supervision to a pretrained robot video world model without replacing its visual VAE.
evidence: DROID-3D achieves under 0.7 px reprojection error on 90% of episodes; depth supervision improves equal-budget RGB PSNR by 1.48 dB.

claim_checks.claim: DROID-3D achieves under 0.7 px reprojection error on 90% of episodes; depth supervision improves equal-budget RGB PSNR by 1.48 dB.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Provides CameraCalibration, MetricDepth, Extrinsics, ReprojectionError, MultiViewFuture, and geometry-consistency fields.

paper_cards.title: LIVIN: Benchmarking Spatial and Embodied Intelligence in Digital Twins of Lived-In Homes
paper_cards.data: Digital twins of 30 diverse lived-in homes preserving layouts, furniture, belongings, and constrained interaction regions.
paper_cards.method: Human-in-the-loop instance recognition, architectural reconstruction, object generation, and placement, with review against source observations.
paper_cards.task: Evaluate 3D detection, reconstruction, navigation, and loco-manipulation in realistic lived-in homes.
paper_cards.novelty: Combines real-home correspondence, interaction readiness, and dense lived-in arrangements in one digital-twin benchmark.
evidence: The benchmark exposes large drops under dense objects, occlusion, limited free space, and constrained interaction regions across four task families.

claim_checks.claim: The benchmark exposes large drops under dense objects, occlusion, limited free space, and constrained interaction regions across four task families.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct infrastructure for HomeTwin, ObjectArrangement, FreeSpace, InteractionRegion, Reconstruction, Navigation, and LocoManipulation schemas.

paper_cards.title: MultiWorldBench: Do Independently Controlled Views Describe One Shared World?
paper_cards.data: 495 Minecraft case configurations across seven suites and ten multiplayer world-consistency capabilities.
paper_cards.method: Diagnostic automatic and human evaluation of control, cross-view motion, shared state, persistence, concurrency, delayed revisit, and structure.
paper_cards.task: Measure whether independently controlled generated views remain one coherent shared world.
paper_cards.novelty: Separates plausible single views from persistent multi-client world consistency with capability-level diagnostics.
evidence: Generated systems score at most 8.00 on persistence and 1.33 on structural consistency versus 91.69 overall for engine ground truth.

claim_checks.claim: Generated systems score at most 8.00 on persistence and 1.33 on structural consistency versus 91.69 overall for engine ground truth.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Essential evaluation layer for SharedState, Persistence, ConcurrentInteraction, CrossViewMotion, DelayedRevisit, and StructuralConsistency.

paper_cards.title: OpenViTac: Learning and Benchmarking Visuo-Tactile Policies in a Unified Sim-and-Real Framework
paper_cards.data: 11 simulation tasks, eight paired real tasks, four tactile capabilities, and three tactile-sensor types.
paper_cards.method: A paired sim-real benchmark plus OpenVTLA, which prepends temporally encoded tactile tokens to a pretrained VLA visual sequence.
paper_cards.task: Evaluate and train VLA, WAM, and VTLA policies on contact-rich manipulation in simulation and reality.
paper_cards.novelty: Provides aligned sim-real tactile tasks and controlled comparisons of tactile representations, fusion, and co-training.
evidence: The official page reports 68.7% simulated and 54.6% real success, 0.913 sim-real correlation, and +15 points from sim co-training on two tasks.

claim_checks.claim: The official page reports 68.7% simulated and 54.6% real success, 0.913 sim-real correlation, and +15 points from sim co-training on two tasks.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct source for TactileHistory, PhysicalProperty, SensorType, SimRealPair, ContactTask, and cross-domain evaluation.

paper_cards.title: RT-Safe: Benchmarking Agent Safety in Real-Time Embodied Environment
paper_cards.data: Simulated urban navigation tasks with moving actors, hazards, traffic rules, and worlds that evolve during inference.
paper_cards.method: Matched static and real-time evaluation explicitly measures both decision safety and latency-induced risk; the benchmark also supports offline RL.
paper_cards.task: Evaluate embodied-agent safety when the physical world continues changing during reasoning and execution.
paper_cards.novelty: Makes inference latency itself part of the embodied safety environment instead of freezing the world at observation time.
evidence: The paper reports only 0.7% safe completion in the hardest setting and 12.3x more collisions in real-time than matched static evaluation.

claim_checks.claim: The paper reports only 0.7% safe completion in the hardest setting and 12.3x more collisions in real-time than matched static evaluation.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Adds ObservationTime, DecisionLatency, ExecutionTime, DynamicHazard, CollisionEvent, and SafeCompletion fields.

paper_cards.title: The Robot Is Not Its Description: GaugeBench for Representation Robustness in Morphology-Aware Policies
paper_cards.data: Physically equivalent rewrites of 80 familiar and 98 held-out robot mechanisms across MetaMorph, ModuMorph, and PyBullet.
paper_cards.method: Rewrites axis direction, angle zero, link/joint ordering, and coordinates while verifying the physical mechanism and policy interface remain equivalent.
paper_cards.task: Test whether morphology-aware policies preserve behavior under equivalent robot-description conventions.
paper_cards.novelty: Separates embodiment generalization from arbitrary representation-gauge robustness.
evidence: MetaMorph return falls from 4030.6 to 51.6 under equivalent descriptions; axis-convention training raises retained return from 3.6% to 80.6%.

claim_checks.claim: MetaMorph return falls from 4030.6 to 51.6 under equivalent descriptions; axis-convention training raises retained return from 3.6% to 80.6%.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct validator for EmbodimentDescription, JointAxis, CoordinateConvention, LinkOrder, ActionTransport, and invariance tests.

paper_cards.title: BiGym 2.0: Benchmarking Learned and Agent-Developed Policies for Humanoid Household Manipulation
paper_cards.data: 20 Unitree G1 household tasks, 60 VR demonstrations per task, 1,200 demonstrations, and 5,400 coding-agent evaluation episodes.
paper_cards.method: A common whole-body controller and observation/action interface compare VLA fine-tuning, imitation, demo-driven RL, and code-writing agents under fixed seeds.
paper_cards.task: Benchmark learned and agent-authored humanoid household manipulation policies.
paper_cards.novelty: Places coding-agent policies and learned humanoid controllers in the same open, replayable evaluation harness.
evidence: The open release includes code, 20 tasks, 1,200 demonstrations, 5,400 agent episodes, and browser-based 3D replay.

claim_checks.claim: The open release includes code, 20 tasks, 1,200 demonstrations, 5,400 agent episodes, and browser-based 3D replay.

limitations: Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
Coverage is bounded by the reported tasks and embodiments.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Strong infrastructure for WholeBodyController, VRDemonstration, HiddenSeed, AgentWrittenPolicy, ReplayTrace, and humanoid task evaluation.
